items.followUp: Define bus topology and name one advantage of it.

rubric.why: A star topology is distinguished by its central connecting device and the way devices connect to it.
rubric.description: Identifies a central hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying the central device and stating that each device connects to it; award 1 mark for only one of these points.

rubric.why: Each device has a separate link to the central device.
rubric.description: States that each device has a separate point-to-point connection to the hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this connection arrangement.

rubric.why: The central device is the defining feature of this layout.
rubric.description: Makes clear that devices communicate through the central device rather than connecting directly to one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the central role of the hub or switch.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, all computers and other devices are connected to one central device, such as a hub or switch.
Each device has a separate point-to-point connection to the central device.
Devices communicate with one another through this central device.

items.followUp: Explain how data travels in a bus topology.

rubric.why: Communication in a star network passes through its central device.
rubric.description: States that the sending device transmits data to the hub or switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the central device as the first destination for data.

rubric.why: The central device handles onward transmission of the data.
rubric.description: Explains that the hub or switch sends the data onward toward the intended device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing onward transmission.

rubric.why: A hub and a switch can handle the onward transmission differently.
rubric.description: Correctly describes broadcasting by a hub or forwarding by a switch.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct distinction.

rubric.why: The central device is a key dependency of the network.
rubric.description: Notes that failure of the central device disrupts communication across the network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this consequence.

modelAnswer: The sending device sends data to the central hub or switch.
A hub sends the data to all connected devices; a switch forwards it to the intended device.
The receiving device accepts the data addressed to it.
If the central device fails, communication across the network is disrupted.

items.followUp: Name and briefly explain the three main goals of information security.

rubric.why: Confidentiality protects information from unauthorised disclosure.
rubric.description: Defines confidentiality as allowing only authorised people to access or view data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying and correctly explaining confidentiality.

rubric.why: Integrity protects the accuracy and completeness of data.
rubric.description: Explains that data should not be altered or damaged without authorisation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying and correctly explaining integrity.

rubric.why: Availability ensures authorised users can access data when needed.
rubric.description: Explains that data and services should be accessible to authorised users when required.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying and correctly explaining availability.

rubric.why: The answer should connect the aspects to the purpose of protecting data.
rubric.description: States that these aspects are goals or requirements for securing data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for clearly linking the aspects to data security.

modelAnswer: The main aspects of data security are confidentiality, integrity and availability.
Confidentiality means that only authorised people can access or view the data.
Integrity means that data remains accurate and complete and is not changed without permission.
Availability means that authorised users can access the data when they need it.

items.followUp: Write two disadvantages of using pseudocode.

rubric.why: A valid disadvantage earns credit.
rubric.description: Gives one valid disadvantage of flowcharts, such as being time-consuming to draw or difficult to modify.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one distinct, valid disadvantage.

rubric.why: A second distinct disadvantage is required.
rubric.description: Gives a second valid disadvantage of flowcharts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct disadvantage; do not award again for a repeated point.

modelAnswer: Flowcharts can take a long time to draw, especially for large problems.
They can be difficult to modify because changes may require redrawing parts of the chart.

items.followUp: What is a candidate solution in problem solving?

rubric.why: A candidate solution is one possible answer being considered for a problem.
rubric.description: Defines a candidate solution as a possible or proposed solution to a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition.

rubric.why: A candidate solution must be checked to determine whether it solves the problem.
rubric.description: States that the proposed solution is tested against the problem's requirements or constraints.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining how it is evaluated.

modelAnswer: A candidate solution is a possible solution proposed for a problem.
It is tested against the problem's requirements or constraints to check whether it works.

items.followUp: Explain the problem-solving strategy called “work backwards.”

rubric.why: Acting out is a way to represent a problem situation directly.
rubric.description: Explains that “act it out” means physically performing or role-playing the situation, or using a physical model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the method.

rubric.why: The purpose is to follow the situation and observe what happens to reach a solution.
rubric.description: States that the actions or steps are followed and their results observed to help solve the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining how the method helps find an answer.

modelAnswer: “Act it out” is a problem-solving strategy in which the situation is physically performed or role-played.
Following the steps and observing what happens can help reveal the solution.

rubric.why: A web page is a document or information resource on the Web.
rubric.description: Identifies a web page as a document or resource containing information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this description.

rubric.why: A web page is accessed on the World Wide Web using a browser and its address.
rubric.description: States that it is viewed using a web browser or accessed using a web address (URL).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either access detail.

modelAnswer: A web page is a document or information resource available on the World Wide Web.
It can be viewed using a web browser and is usually accessed through its URL.

rubric.why: Repeated division by 16 produces the hexadecimal digits as remainders.
rubric.description: Shows a correct repeated-division step or the corresponding sequence of remainders.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct division step or correct remainder sequence.

rubric.why: Reading the remainders from bottom to top gives the hexadecimal representation.
rubric.description: Gives the correct hexadecimal result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Divide repeatedly by 16: 69610 ÷ 16 = 4350 remainder 10 (A).
271 ÷ 16 = 16 remainder 15 (F).
16 ÷ 16 = 1 remainder 0.
1 ÷ 16 = 0 remainder 1.
Read the remainders from bottom to top: (69610)₁₀ = (10FEA)₁₆.
